question: A launcher takes the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0 and adds 11 to it, reading the result as a release speed in metres per second. A puck of mass 13 kg is released at that speed along a level air table, and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. A trigger coil adds 18 J to that figure and a damper then absorbs 17 J. The table is 1.6 m wide. What energy remains, in J?

A cam gives the follower displacement as 3 times the cube of the shaft angle minus 5 times the square of the shaft angle. The rate at which that displacement is changing at a shaft angle of 2.0 has 9 added to it, and the result is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a slide whose mass is 124000 g. The force the drive must apply to the slide to accelerate it at that rate is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons. A static frame preload of 15 kN is then added. What load does the frame carry, in kN?

A hoist controller adds its two calibration constants 4 and 14, multiplies the sum by 5, and then subtracts 25, reading the result as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A cage of mass 30000 g is lifted with that acceleration and the force the cable must apply to the cage is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons. A static preload of 7 kN is added to it. Because 9 identical cages hang from one headframe, the headframe load is 9 times that total. What is the headframe load, in kN?

Between the 1st and the 3rd second of a cycle, a linear motor advances at a rate equal to 4 times the square of the elapsed time plus 2 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that interval, taken as a plain number, is the release speed in metres per second of a carriage whose mass is 39 kg. The energy the carriage carries because of its motion is recorded and a trigger coil adds 14 J to it. That figure is expressed in kilojoules and a damper then absorbs 12 kJ. What energy remains, in kJ?

The figure the report ends on is 6 kJ less than 4 times the kilojoule reading described below. A launch controller adds its two dial settings 2 and 15 and multiplies the sum by 4 to fix the release speed, in metres per second, of a sled whose mass is 50 kg. The sled runs along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules to give that reading. The rail is 40 m long. What figure does the report end on, in kJ?

The number the rig records at the end is 9 N more than the force described below. A cam on a press gives the follower displacement as 5 times the cube of the crank angle plus 5 times the square of the crank angle, and the rate at which the rate of change of that displacement is itself changing, at a crank angle of 1.0, is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a slide whose mass is 105 kg. The force the drive must apply to the slide to accelerate it at that rate is calculated, tripled because 3 slides share a frame, and multiplied by 12 because 12 such frames stand in the hall, which gives the force in question. The press runs at 140 rpm. What number does the rig record, in N?

The number the sheet ends on is 22 J less than a figure that is 18 J above a value 8 J below the energy described here. A cam gives the follower displacement as 5 times the cube of the shaft angle minus 4 times the square of the shaft angle, and the rate at which that displacement is changing at a shaft angle of 2.0 is the release speed in metres per second of a slider whose mass is 2 kg. The energy the slider carries because of its motion is the energy in question. The shaft turns at 240 rpm. What number does the sheet end on, in J?

The figure the bench prints last is the kilojoule form of the joule tally described below. A launcher takes the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 11x + 24 = 0 and reads it as a release speed in metres per second. A slug of mass 10000 g is released at that speed along a level rail, and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. A trigger coil adds 17 J to that reading and a damper then absorbs 2 J, which gives the joule tally in question. What figure does the bench print last, in kJ?

The number the day sheet ends with is 9 times a value that is itself 8 times the joule tally described below. A test bench takes the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0 and reads it as the release speed in metres per second of a trolley whose mass is 14000 g. The trolley runs along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. A trigger coil adds 24 J to that reading and a brake then removes 11 J, which gives the tally in question. What number does the day sheet end with, in J?

A cam gives the follower displacement as 2 times the cube of the crank angle plus 1 times the square of the crank angle. The rate at which that displacement is changing at a crank angle of 1.0 is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a slide whose mass is 179000 g. The force the drive must apply to the slide to accelerate it at that rate is calculated, a preload of 21 N is added to it, and a further 26 N of clamp force is added after that. Because 11 identical slides run from one frame, and 6 such frames stand in the hall, the hall load is that figure multiplied by 11 and then by 6. The crank turns at 95 rpm. What is the hall load, in N?

A launcher takes the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 14x + 48 = 0 and reads it as a release speed in metres per second. A dart of mass 33000 g is released at that speed along a level rail, and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. The rig fires 7 darts in a magazine and their energies add, and 7 identical magazines are emptied in the trial with those energies adding too. What is the trial total, in kJ?

A test track launches a small instrumented puck along a level rail. The engineers set the puck speed in m/s by adding together all the whole numbers from 1 to 10 and then subtracting 6 from that total. The puck has a mass of 5000 g. The track itself is 40 m long, a figure the timing team records but does not use here. The lab reports the energy carried by the moving puck in kJ rather than in J. Because 9 identical pucks are launched in the same run, the report gives 9 times the single-puck figure. What total energy in kJ is reported?

A wind tunnel team must publish one number: the final rig load in kN. The carriage under test has a mass of 186000 g. A calibration curve stored in the controller is 3*x**3 + 5*x**2, and the slope of that curve at x = 2 is the first quantity the software reads. The carriage acceleration in m/s^2 is that slope plus 21. The force the carriage then experiences is converted to kN, a fixed offset of 26 is added to that kN figure, and the sum is multiplied by 6 because 6 carriages share the same frame. What is the final rig load in kN?

A crane workshop wants the single hook load in N that ends its checklist. The hoisted block has a mass of 170 kg. Its acceleration in m/s^2 is the area under the curve 1*x**2 + 4*x between x = 3 and x = 4. The workshop hoists 4 such blocks on one hook, so the hook carries 4 times the force needed for one block. The checklist then adds 8 N for the sling, adds 25 N for the spreader beam, and subtracts 10 N for a buoyancy allowance in the wash tank. What hook load in N ends the checklist?

A robotics bench pushes a sled along a polished track. Two encoder wheels on the drive carry 147 and 89 teeth, and the firmware sets the sled acceleration in m/s^2 equal to the largest whole number that divides both tooth counts exactly. The sled has a mass of 148000 g. The force on the sled is reported in kN rather than in N. From that kN figure the bench subtracts 4 for the cable drag calibration. The result is then multiplied by 6 because 6 identical benches run in parallel. What value in kN does the parallel bank report?

A hydro test rig closes its report with one energy figure in kJ. The rig drives a ram of mass 34 kg. Two gear trains carry 207 and 306 teeth, and the ram speed in m/s is set to the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The rig fires 11 rams per cycle and runs 3 cycles per test, so the energy the moving ram carries is multiplied by 11 and then by 3. The hydraulic reservoir holds 250 L, a figure printed on the rig plate but not needed here. The report finally multiplies the kJ total by 8 because 8 rigs are installed. What energy in kJ closes the report?

A lift-testing company must state the final shaft load in kN. The test mass carried on the car is 115000 g. Its acceleration in m/s^2 is the larger of the two values of x for which x**2 - 14*x + 48 comes to 0. Once the force on the test mass is written in kN, the company subtracts 12 for the counterweight credit. It then adds 23 for the guide-rail reaction, and adds 11 more for the buffer preload. What is the final shaft load in kN?

A conveyor lab launches a carrier block of mass 59000 g along a rail. Two drive sprockets have 16 and 44 teeth, and the block speed in m/s is set to the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The lab records the energy carried by the moving block in kJ rather than in J. To that kJ figure a fixed allowance of 30 is added for the drive train. The sum is then multiplied by 6 because 6 carriers run on the loop. Finally 20 is subtracted for the regenerative braking credit. What figure in kJ does the lab record?

A ski-lift workshop tests a gondola dummy of mass 43 kg on a launch cradle. The cradle speed in m/s is the area under the curve 1*x**2 + 6*x between x = 2 and x = 3. To the energy the moving dummy carries, the workshop adds 2 J to account for the cradle spring. The cradle rail is 18 m long, which is noted on the drawing but not needed here. The total is then written in kJ, and 1 is subtracted from that kJ figure for the instrumentation offset. Because 12 gondolas are tested in a batch, the result is multiplied by 12. What energy in kJ does the workshop report for the batch?

A pneumatic launcher on a lab bench propels a puck of mass 3000 g. The puck speed in m/s is the area under the curve 3*x**2 + 1*x between x = 1 and x = 4. The bench air supply sits at 7 bar, a reading logged for the record but not used in this calculation. The launcher fires 8 pucks in one burst, so the burst carries 8 times the energy of a single moving puck. The technician then adds 19 J for the trigger solenoid. Because 6 launchers run together, the final figure is 6 times that sum. What energy in J does the bank of launchers deliver?

A test-stand controller drives a shuttle of mass 60 kg along a track. A stored profile is 2*x**3 - 5*x**2, and the slope of that profile at x = 2 is read off first. The shuttle speed in m/s is 8 times that slope. From the energy the moving shuttle carries, the controller subtracts 23 J for guide friction. The stand runs 6 shuttles at once, so the total is 6 times that corrected value. A final 24 J is subtracted for the brake resistor loss. What energy in J does the controller log?

A ballistics bench closes its data sheet with one energy figure in kJ. The projectile it fires has a mass of 34000 g. A stored charge curve is 2*x**2 + 0*x, and the area under it between x = 0 and x = 1 is the first number the software computes. The projectile speed in m/s is 12 times that area. The barrel is 3 m long, a figure on the bench label that does not enter the calculation. To the energy the moving projectile carries the bench adds 29 J for the sabot, converts the total to kJ, and multiplies it by 2 because 2 barrels fire together. What energy in kJ closes the data sheet?

A theme-park ride shop must publish one energy figure in J for a launch bank. Each launch car has a mass of 54000 g. The car speed in m/s is 8 times the larger of the two values of x that make x**2 - 4*x + 3 equal to 0. To the energy carried by one moving car the shop adds 21 J for the launch fin. A train holds 5 cars, so the train figure is 5 times that. The bank runs 10 trains, so the published number is 10 times the train figure. What energy in J is published?

A test cell reports one clamp force in kN at the end of its run sheet. The specimen carrier has a mass of 18000 g. Its acceleration in m/s^2 is the area under the curve 5*x**2 + 8*x between x = 1 and x = 2. Once the force on the carrier is expressed in kN, the cell adds 20 for the hydraulic preload. The sheet then multiplies that sum by 10 because 10 clamps act on the specimen. What clamp force in kN does the run sheet report?

A rolling mill logs one energy figure in kJ for each coil pass. The pusher block has a mass of 39 kg. A stored cam profile is 2*x**3 - 6*x**2, and its slope at x = 3 is read first; the pusher speed in m/s is that slope plus 17. The mill floor is kept at 22 degrees C, a value in the log header that does not enter the calculation. The energy the moving block carries is written in kJ and then multiplied by 10 for the 10 passes in a coil. Finally 19 is subtracted from that kJ figure for the drive regeneration credit. What energy in kJ is logged for the coil?
